transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-23 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Evan Liu (Redwood SE) — Maya Patel (Veridian Head of AI), Luis Ramirez (Platform Engineer), Danielle Cole (CISO), Omar Aziz (PM)

Summary (auto): QBR + health check; usage up 32% q/q, cost overrun on peak hours, two infra incidents (brief outage during model rollout), customer exploring Dedicated or Private for compliance and stable latency. Action items and benchmarks agreed.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — this is the QBR for Veridian, appreciate you all making time. Quick check — can everyone see the shared deck? I posted a link in chat, /docs/qbr-veridian-jul-2026.pdf
00:14 Maya: Yep, can see it. Thanks Jordan.
00:18 Jordan: Cool. We'll run through usage, costs, incidents, then open to roadmap and dev questions. Priya will cover adoption and health metrics, Evan will go into the infra and latency details.
00:30 Priya: Quick numbers — monthly tokens up ~32% q/q, active routes increased from 8 to 12, embeddings usage steady. Biggest growth on the triage assistant route during morning peak. Cost-wise your hosted spend is also up ~28% because peak tail tokens and some cache misses.
00:55 Luis: Right, we noticed the cost spike correlates with peak 9am–11am PST. We tried increasing batching on our side but saw higher latencies — so we backed off.
01:12 Evan: Mm-hmm, that's expected; the latency vs cost tradeoff shows up when you push batching too high without proper autoscaling. On Dedicated you can get more predictable p95 by reserving capacity and tuning batch size.
01:28 Maya: Can you remind us quickly the difference between Dedicated and Private? We flagged Private because of PHI concerns.
01:35 Jordan: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in Redwood's managed infra with isolation and SLA; Private is customer VPC / on-prem option where control plane is private and you manage networking, KMS, etc. For PHI we'd usually recommend Private or at least Dedicated with strict encryption and KMS.
01:50 Danielle: On that note, we need details about encryption at rest and KMS key rotation. Is that in the security pack?
01:58 Jordan: Yes, I posted SOC2 + KMS integration notes earlier, /docs/security-summary.pdf — we'll also send the full security binder after the call.
02:10 Danielle: Perfect.
02:12 Evan: Quick note on the outage — on 2026-06-16 we saw a brief rollback during a canary rollout; root cause was a model variant mismatch in the routing policy which caused synthetic traffic to fill a fallback pool. It lasted ~7 minutes and increased error rates. We implemented a guardrail in routing configs and added more robust health checks to prevent identical regressions.
02:40 Luis: That matches our incident log, thanks. What are the mitigations for us while we decide on Dedicated? We're sensitive to p95 spikes.
02:48 Evan: We recommend three short-term steps: 1) enable prefix/KV caching on your chat flows (we saw cache hit rates under 40% for a few routes), 2) adjust routing policy to overflow to a slightly higher-latency but cheaper model instead of full erroring, 3) temporary reserved burst capacity during morning peak — we can propose a small commit for guaranteed throughput.
03:10 Maya: How much would that reserved burst roughly cost? We ran an estimate and it's a bit fuzzy.
03:16 Jordan: I'll send a sizing + pricing proposal but ballpark for your 20% peak headroom it's roughly $X/month (see pricing sheet) — I'll add a concrete number in the follow-up.
03:30 Priya: Also, usage optimizations — we have a set of recommended quantization profiles that cut per-token cost by ~15% for certain models without measurable quality loss. Evan, I can share the guide.
03:41 Evan: Yes we have a quantization/quality matrix; we'll run a quick eval on your prompt set to validate.
03:48 Omar: About the evals — can you run them on a copy of our prompt sets? We prefer not to send live user data.
03:55 Evan: Absolutely, we can run benchmarks against masked or synthetic prompt sets. That will give us latency/cost tradeoffs and quality deltas.
04:05 Maya: On the roadmap piece — we want clearer rollout windows for the next two quarters. We're aiming for an enterprise go-live for two new assistants in Q4, which will double concurrency.
04:18 Jordan: That's good to know. We should start a capacity planning thread. I can include recommended Dedicated pool sizes and autoscale policies in the proposal.
04:27 Priya: I'll also sync with your product team on feature adoption and create a baseline success metric set — e.g., 99% availability during core hours, p95 under 600ms for assistant X, cost per 1k tokens under $Y.
04:41 Danielle: The availability SLO is critical; any SLA language around that for Dedicated?
04:47 Jordan: Dedicated has SLA targets we can include; for Private it's more depends-on-customer infra but we can offer a support commitment. We'll share the SLA doc.
04:55 Luis: Security question — how do audit logs get forwarded? We need immutable logs for compliance.
05:01 Evan: We support log forwarding to your SIEM via secure syslog/HTTPS and can ship audit logs to your S3 with retention policies. For Private we can keep logs in your VPC.
05:10 Danielle: Good. Also, SSO/SAML mapping — do you expose SCIM for provisioning roles?
05:16 Jordan: Yes, SCIM and SAML SSO with RBAC present; we'll include sample configs in the security docs.
05:23 Maya: Can you summarize the two paths you recommend? Quick bullet points.
05:27 Evan: Path A (near-term): stay Hosted + small reserved burst + caching/quantization + routing guards. Path B (mid-term): Dedicated reservation for predictable p95 and capacity; Path C (if PHI + strict controls): Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and VPC.
05:45 Omar: Timeline for Path B adoption — how long to migrate?
05:50 Jordan: For Dedicated it's typically 2–4 weeks of provisioning and testing; for Private it's 6–10 weeks depending on network and KMS integration and on-prem packaging.
06:03 Maya: Budget question — if we commit to Dedicated, do we get discounted token pricing?
06:09 Jordan: Yes, commit-based pricing for Dedicated; we'll include tiers in the follow-up proposal.
06:15 Priya: Another operational note — we'll enable per-route tracing and the Redwood Console dashboard for your SREs so you can track token costs down to caller.
06:28 Luis: That will help. One more thing — can we run an A/B on fallback models? We want to keep UX but cut 20% cost.
06:36 Evan: Sure, we can do canary rollouts and A/B experiments with automatic fallback policies. We'll include sample configs.
06:44 Maya: OK thanks. Danielle, any compliance blockers you want to call out now?
06:49 Danielle: Mainly PHI handling and key management; also retention windows for PII. I will send the detailed checklist to Priya by end of next week.
06:58 Priya: Noted. We'll treat that as a priority.
07:02 Jordan: Quick recap of agreed next steps — Jordan to send pricing + reserve proposal; Evan to run benchmarks; Priya to set up monthly dashboard; Danielle to send compliance checklist. Any objections?
07:16 Maya: No objections. Thanks.
07:18 Omar: Please include a proposed pilot plan for Dedicated — small commit, 4-week trial, success criteria.
07:26 Jordan: Will do.
07:28 Maya: Thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and minor clarifications; timestamps omitted for brevity but total talk aligns with 45m duration)

Key artifacts referenced: /docs/qbr-veridian-jul-2026.pdf, /docs/security-summary.pdf, pricing spreadsheet (shared in chat), benchmark spreadsheet (to be uploaded).

End meeting: 16:45 UTC
